questions.q: Which two tenses may never appear after conditional « si » ?
choices: The pluperfect and the past conditional
questions.why: After si you may write the present, the imperfect or the pluperfect, and nothing else. Si j'aurais su is the textbook example of bad French; the correct form is si j'avais su.

questions.q: Say this out loud: if you want, we can leave.
questions.target: si tu veux, on peut partir
questions.why: Type 1, the everyday one: si plus the present, with the present, future or imperative in the other half.

questions.q: Type 1: « S'il ___ (pleuvoir), je resterai à la maison. »
questions.why: The main clause may be in the future, but the si clause stays in the present. Note s' before il: the elision happens only before il and ils.

questions.q: Type 2: « Si j'___ (avoir) de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison. »
questions.why: Unreal present: si plus the imperfect, with the present conditional opposite. The imperfect here has nothing to do with the past — it is just what the pattern requires.

questions.q: Type 2, other half: « Si tu venais, on ___ (être) content. »
questions.why: Imperfect in the si half forces the present conditional in the main half. Never the reverse.

questions.q: Type 3: « Si j'___ (savoir), je serais venu. »
questions.why: Unreal past: si plus the pluperfect, with the past conditional opposite. This is the tense of regret — it did not happen and it is too late.

questions.q: Type 3, other half: « Si tu m'avais appelé, j'___ (répondre). »
questions.why: Pluperfect in the si half, past conditional in the main half. Répondre takes avoir, and there is no preceding direct object, so the participle stays flat.

questions.q: Which pairing is a real French pattern?
questions.why: The three legal rows are: présent → présent/futur/impératif, imparfait → conditionnel présent, plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé. There is no French subjunctive after si, ever.

questions.q: « Si j'étais toi, je ne dirais rien. » What is « étais » here?
choices: A subjunctive, matching English if I were
The ordinary imperfect, which is simply what type 2 requires
A past tense — it is about something that used to be true
A mistake for si je serais
questions.why: English marks this with a special subjunctive form, were. French just uses the imperfect, and that trap catches English speakers constantly.

questions.q: Is « Je ne sais pas s'il viendra » correct?
choices: No — si never takes the future
Yes — here si means whether, and the ban does not apply
No — it should be s'il vienne
questions.why: The ban on the future applies only to conditional si. If you can substitute whether in English, the future is allowed: s'il viendra, je serai content would be wrong, because there si means if.

questions.q: Which type is « Si j'avais étudié, je parlerais français maintenant » ?
choices: Mixed: a past condition with a present result
questions.why: The halves keep their own logic. A pluperfect condition can carry a present conditional result, and the reverse also works: si j'étais plus organisé, j'aurais fini hier.

questions.q: Which tense follows « au cas où » ?
questions.why: Au cas où is the one if-like expression that takes the conditional: au cas où il pleuvrait, prends un parapluie. À condition que and à moins que take the subjunctive; même si takes the indicative.

questions.q: Build the sentence: I'll stay home if it rains.
questions.why: Either half may come first; only the comma changes, and with the main clause first there is none. The future stays out of the si half.
Type 2 in its purest form: imperfect after si, present conditional after the comma.

questions.q: Write out the three si-patterns as a table: which tense goes in each half, and what each means.
a: 1. Real: si + présent → présent, futur or impératif. It may well happen: S'il pleut, je resterai à la maison. 2. Unreal present: si + imparfait → conditionnel présent. It isn't so, but imagine: Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison. 3. Unreal past: si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé. It didn't happen: Si j'avais su, je serais venu.
questions.why: Three rows, learned once, and conditionals stop being a problem. The one thing to carry above all: no future and no conditional after si.
